key_insight: Federated breast imaging models showed strong normal-versus-sick discrimination, but acquisition-year confounding calls into question whether they learned pathology.
clinical_relevance: This imaging study—not drug discovery—does not establish reliable benign-versus-malignant discrimination or clinical readiness.
method: Compared CLIP, BiomedCLIP, and an ImageNet-pretrained vision transformer using federated learning on two public breast imaging datasets.
Evaluated client-level differential privacy and a CLIP ablation without the text pathway.
Measured patient-level ROC-AUC, bootstrap confidence intervals, threshold sensitivity, model agreement, and communication cost.
evidence_signal: Normal-versus-sick ROC-AUC was 0.940–0.990, versus 0.974 for acquisition year alone; benign-versus-malignant ROC-AUC was 0.504–0.637, with all 95% confidence intervals including 0.50.
watch_item: Differential privacy reduced ROC-AUC by 0.375 when applied to the full model state rather than only trainable parameters, highlighting implementation sensitivity.
paper_title: Evaluating Federated Vision-Language and Vision-Only Models for Privacy-Aware Breast Cancer Imaging
